summary:
I made a read-only inventory of the GNOME Settings 50 panels assigned to this step (installed gnome-control-center 1:50.3-0ubuntu0.2, gnome-settings-daemon 50.0, gnome-shell 50.1). There are 212 items, covering every user-visible setting or action with its backing. Nothing talked to the live session.

**How I checked.** The labels come from the UI files built into /usr/bin/gnome-control-center. I extracted them with `gresource extract` into /tmp/claude-1000/-home-robin-Documents-Codex-2026-11-01-chat-outputs-win11-gnome/b86efb11-6e95-47e6-8bcd-969df897e3ac/scratchpad/ui/. Keys, types, ranges, enums and defaults come from /usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas/*.gschema.xml plus the installed overrides (mainly 10_ubuntu-settings and 10_ubuntu-dock). D-Bus APIs come from /usr/share/dbus-1/interfaces/*.xml and strings in the service binaries, and polkit actions from /usr/share/polkit-1/actions. Preset lists are as the UI shows them: number-row values from the UI XML, and the suspend delays from a table in the binary (900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2700, 3600, 4800, 5400, 6000, 7200 s). Two values are not confirmed: the cursor-size list (I give 24/32/48/64/96 from GNOME's code) and the exact meaning of the stylus 'default' button action.

**Ubuntu 26.04 differences.**
- **Overrides:** power-button-action='interactive', sleep-inactive-ac-timeout=0, sound theme 'Yaru', DING start-corner 'bottom-right', and the dock set to fixed, panel mode, on the left.
- **Ubuntu-only pages:** Lock Screen on Suspend (ubuntu-lock-on-suspend), Telemetry (whoopsie and ubuntu-insights), Security Center, Startup Sound (org.gnome.shell.ubuntu startup-sound='warty-startup') and the Ubuntu Desktop panel. That panel now has only Desktop Icons, Dock and Enhanced Tiling; appearance and accent colour moved to the Appearance panel.
- **Hidden here:** some rows don't show on this machine because a package is missing or the hardware isn't there:
  - packages not installed: gnome-user-share (File Sharing), openssh-server (Secure Shell), malcontent-control (Parental Controls), realmd (Enterprise Login), usbguard (Forbid New USB Devices);
  - hardware-dependent: Thunderbolt, privacy screen, light sensor and battery rows.
- **Not in GNOME 50 Privacy:** the Microphone page is gone. The disable-microphone key still exists, so I listed it because Windows 11 has a Microphone page.

**Design constraints.** Everything is GSettings, D-Bus or polkit, so it all fits GTK 4 + Rust:
- **Online Accounts** can link libgoa-backend-1.0 (GTK 4 + libadwaita, no WebKit; OAuth goes through the external browser).
- **Printers** use cups-pk-helper. They also use system-config-printer's D-Bus service for drivers; that service is Python, but it runs as an existing system service, not inside WinPoint.
- **System changes** each go through the polkit action that GNOME itself uses.
- **External apps:** Orca's configuration, language-selector, update-manager and desktop-security-center are separate apps GNOME launches; WinPoint can launch them the same way.

**WinPoint today.** Of these functions WinPoint covers:
- Power: idle-delay, idle-dim, sleep-inactive-* and the power profile.
- Sound: output volume and sink.
- Battery status, Clear History and Empty Trash.
- Its own copies, not the GNOME keys: notification do-not-disturb, text size, 24-hour clock and show-seconds.
- About: partial.

Missing entirely: Printers, Users/sign-in, Online Accounts, Sharing and Remote Desktop, Secure Shell, Search, Graphics Tablets, Wellbeing, most of Privacy (screen lock, location, camera, telemetry, Thunderbolt, device security), most of Accessibility, Region/login-screen locale and the Date & Time writes.

**Where it goes in Windows 11.** Each item's notes give the suggested page and nl-NL wording (Win11:). In short:
- System: Notifications, Power & battery, Sound, Remote Desktop, About.
- Accounts: Email & accounts, Your info, Sign-in options, Other users, Family.
- Bluetooth & devices: Printers & scanners, Pen & Windows Ink.
- Privacy & security: Location, Camera, Diagnostics & feedback, Search permissions, Searching Windows, Windows Security; Storage Sense for trash and temp files.
- Time & language: Date & time, Language & region, including administrative language settings for the login screen.
- Accessibility: text size, visual effects, mouse pointer, magnifier, audio, keyboard, mouse, colour filters.
- Personalisation: Taskbar, desktop icons; Multitasking: snap windows.
- Wellbeing has no Settings counterpart in Windows 11; it fits under System > Focus or Accounts > Family.

**Mouse.** You named mouse settings as missing. The gnome-mouse-panel itself was not in this step's list, but I saw its UI while extracting. It has primary button left/right, pointer speed, mouse acceleration, scroll direction, a touchpad tab (on/off, disable while typing, speed, secondary click, tap to click, scroll method and direction), a pointing-stick tab and Test Settings, all backed by org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.mouse/touchpad/pointingstick. It must be covered by whichever step owns the mouse panel. The mouse-related accessibility options (double-click delay, mouse keys, locate pointer, hover click) are in this list under universal-access.
